sentences.text: Harriotta is a genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the family Rhinochimaeridae, placed within the kingdom Animalia, phylum Chordata, class Chondrichthyes, and order Chimaeriformes.
Species in this genus are commonly known as rabbitfish, spookfish, or chimaera.
The genus Harriotta includes three species: Harriotta avia, Harriotta haeckeli, and Harriotta raleighana.
The species Harriotta avia was described by Finucci, Didier, Ebert, Green, and Kemper in 2024.
The species Harriotta lehmani was described by Werdelin in 1986 from fossils found in Lebanon dating to the Late Cretaceous (Santonian).
The species Harriotta gosseleti was described by Winkler in 1880 from fossils found in Belgium dating to the Oligocene (Rupelian).
The Paleobiology Database records two fossil occurrences for the genus Harriotta.
Living Harriotta species inhabit deep waters of continental slopes between 380 and 2,600 meters deep in the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.
Harriotta species are also found in the Indian Ocean off southern Australia.
Fossil evidence of the genus Harriotta dates from the Coniacian to Santonian stages, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.
